57:  * Description:
58:  *   Bluetooth transport, host registration and (optionally) the GATT
59:  *   fixture.  Deliberately NOT called from bk7258_bringup(): it only needs
60:  *   the mailbox and PWC, which bk7258_bringup() has already finished, and
61:  *   everything it does happens before the panels would otherwise light up.
62:  *   Registering the host cost the boot greeting its head start, and a radio
63:  *   that comes up a moment later is not something a user can see, whereas a
64:  *   screen that stays dark is.  Called from board_late_initialize() after
65:  *   the display instead.

232: /****************************************************************************
233:  * Name: bk7258_report_cache
234:  *
235:  * Description:
236:  *   Reports whether this core implements instruction and data caches, and is
237:  *   left in at boot so the next person does not have to guess.
238:  *
239:  *   The AP executes in place from flash at 0x02150000.  NuttX did not enable
240:  *   the instruction cache until commit "perf(bk7258): enable the AP
241:  *   instruction cache", and every instruction fetch was a flash access: the
242:  *   expression renderer cost ~455ms per frame for work that takes 0.09ms on a
243:  *   host, a 51200-byte word-at-a-time copy ran at 0.8MB/s, and raising the
244:  *   core to 480MHz changed none of it because the core was never the limit.
245:  *   The same frame now costs 37ms.
246:  *
247:  *   Turning it on needed two independent fixes, and the first one alone looks
248:  *   like "the cache does nothing": CONFIG_ARMV8M_ICACHE depends on the hidden
249:  *   ARMV8M_HAVE_ICACHE, which this chip's Kconfig did not select, so asking
250:  *   for it in a defconfig was silently dropped; and selecting it only compiles
251:  *   up_enable_icache() in -- every other ARMv8-M chip in the tree calls that
252:  *   from its own start code, this one did not.  Both are fixed now (see the
253:  *   chip Kconfig and bk7258_start.c).
254:  *
255:  *   Only the I-Cache is on.  Instruction fetch is read-only and needs no
256:  *   maintenance against the camera, panel and mailbox DMA that shares AP RAM,
257:  *   which the MPU deliberately keeps non-cacheable.
258:  *
259:  *   CLIDR/CTR exist in ARMv8-M whether or not a cache is fitted (they read
260:  *   zero when it is not), so reading them is safe and settles the question:
261:  *   this part reports CLIDR=0x09200003, i.e. both caches are implemented.
262:  *
263:  ****************************************************************************/
264: 
265: static void bk7258_report_cache(void)
266: {
267:   uint32_t clidr = getreg32(0xe000ed78);   /* SCB->CLIDR */
268:   uint32_t ctr   = getreg32(0xe000ed7c);   /* SCB->CTR   */
269:   unsigned int l1 = clidr & 7;
270: 
271:   printf("cache: CLIDR=0x%08" PRIx32 " CTR=0x%08" PRIx32
272:          " L1=%s%s%s\n", clidr, ctr,
273:          (l1 & 1) != 0 ? "I" : "",
274:          (l1 & 2) != 0 ? "D" : "",
275:          l1 == 0 ? "none (uncached XIP from flash)" :
276:          (l1 == 3 ? " (separate I and D)" : ""));
277: }
278: 
279: void board_late_initialize(void)
280: {
281:   int ret = bk7258_bringup();
282: 
283:   bk7258_report_cache();
284: 
285:   if (ret < 0)
286:     {
287:       printf("board bring-up stopped, error=%d\n", ret);
288:       return;
289:     }
290: 
291:   printf("board bring-up initialization completed\n");
292: 
293:   /* GC9D01 QSPI panel bring-up smoke test.  board_app_finalinitialize()
294:    * (BOARDIOC_FINALINIT) is never invoked in this minimal, apps-less NSH
295:    * configuration (no CONFIG_BOARDCTL_FINALINIT, no apps/nshlib start-up
296:    * script caller), so the test entry point is invoked here instead, from
297:    * the unconditionally-called CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE hook.  See
298:    * docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-gc9d01-lcd-bringup.md Task 3 Step 3.
299:    */
300: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_GC9D01_FB
301:   /* GC9D01 framebuffers, one per populated panel: fb_register() calls
302:    * up_fbinitialize(), which does the rail/reset/bus bring-up and the init
303:    * sequence and allocates a 51200-byte RGB565 framebuffer, then publishes
304:    * /dev/fb<display>.
305:    *
306:    * Both panels are registered unconditionally.  GC9D01 has no readable ID
307:    * register, so an unpopulated footprint cannot be distinguished from a
308:    * working panel -- every command still "completes".  Registering /dev/fb1
309:    * on a single-panel board therefore costs one unused 51200-byte buffer
310:    * and nothing else; refusing to register it would need board-variant
311:    * configuration that this board provides no way to detect.
312:    */
313: 
314:   {
315:     int display;
316:     int registered = 0;
317: 
318:     /* Both panels through reset and the command table in one pass, before
319:      * fb_register() asks for either of them.  The sequence is nearly all
320:      * waiting (20ms rail, 230ms reset pulse, 120ms after Sleep Out) and the
321:      * waits are the panels', not the bus's, so sharing them across the two
322:      * panels takes ~350ms off the time to the first pixel.  fb_register()
323:      * still calls up_fbinitialize() -> bk7258_gc9d01_panel_init(), which
324:      * finds its panel already up and returns.
325:      */
326: 
327:     (void)bk7258_gc9d01_panels_init((1 << GC9D01_NDISPLAYS) - 1);
328: 
329:     for (display = 0; display < GC9D01_NDISPLAYS; display++)
330:       {
331:         ret = fb_register(display, 0);
332:         if (ret < 0)
333:           {
334:             printf("fb_register(%d) failed: %d\n", display, ret);
335:             continue;
336:           }
337: 
338:         registered |= 1 << display;
339:         printf("fb: /dev/fb%d registered\n", display);
340:       }
341: 
342:     /* Boot greeting, written out rather than simply appearing.
343:      *
344:      * The panel has no readable ID register, so "the init sequence was sent"
345:      * has never been evidence that it worked; something has to be drawn at
346:      * boot or a dead panel looks exactly like a working one.
347:      *
348:      * Both panels are revealed together, one stroke segment per step, so the
349:      * word is written left to right.  The step count is the whole cost: the
350:      * panel takes no partial update, so every step pushes a full 51200-byte
351:      * frame to each panel at ~25ms, and the stroke rendering adds to that.
352:      * 20 steps measured 1677ms and was by itself most of the delay between
353:      * reset and a readable screen; 8 steps measured 408ms on the same board
354:      * and still reads as writing rather than appearing.  Keep it at 8 unless
355:      * there is a measurement to justify more.
356:      *
357:      * The pen-stroke version of this lives in the 'hello' shell command,
358:      * which has a proper stroke font.  It cannot be reused here: it is an
359:      * application, and this configuration builds neither exec_builtin() nor
360:      * posix_spawn(), so bring-up has no way to start it.
361:      */
362: 
363:     if (registered != 0)
364:       {
365:         (void)bk7258_gc9d01_fb_hello_animate(registered, 8);
366:       }
367:   }
368: #endif
369: 
370:   /* GC2145 camera: registered as a standard V4L2 /dev/video0 node here
371:    * (imgdata+imgsensor framework, see bk7258_camera_bringup.c), superseding
372:    * the older bare board_late_initialize() smoke-test call this line used
373:    * to make directly.  The old bk7258_gc2145_test() bare entry point is
374:    * kept as an independent NSH command (see bk7258_appinit.c) for
375:    * side-by-side diagnostic comparison, per design discussion in
376:    * docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-gc2145-camera-bringup.md -- it is
377:    * intentionally NOT called from here anymore, so a bug in this new V4L2
378:    * driver cannot be masked by (or confused with) the old direct-call
379:    * path still running unconditionally at boot. */
380:   (void)bk7258_camera_initialize();
381: 
382: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_AUDIO
383:   /* Internal-DAC audio.  This has to come after bk7258_bringup() above,
384:    * not from inside it, for the same reason the camera does: the AUD block
385:    * needs the AUDP power domain and the AUD module clock, and both are
386:    * requested from CP1 over the PWC mailbox channel that bk7258_pwc_start()
387:    * brings up.  Registering the audio devices is best-effort -- a failure
388:    * here must not take the console down with it.
389:    */
390: 
391:   (void)bk7258_audio_initialize();
392: #endif
393: 
394: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_JPEG_ENC
395:   /* After the camera: both want PSRAM, and registering the encoder second
396:    * keeps /dev/video0 belonging to capture and /dev/video1 to this codec no
397:    * matter how the framework numbers them internally.  Best-effort, like the
398:    * others -- a codec that fails to register must not take the console down.
399:    */
400: 
401:   (void)bk7258_jpeg_enc_initialize();
402: #endif
403: 
404: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_BLUETOOTH
405:   /* Last, so that nothing a user can see waits on the radio.  See
406:    * bk7258_bt_bringup() above for why this is not part of bk7258_bringup().
407:    */
408: 
409:   bk7258_bt_bringup();
410: #endif
411: }

1: /****************************************************************************
2:  * board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_ramdisk.c
3:  *
4:  * PSRAM-backed RAM disk so that captured frames can be written to a real
5:  * file ("file mode" of apps/system/nxcamera's `output <path> [nframes]`).
6:  *
7:  * Why this exists: the only writable filesystem this board had was tmpfs,
8:  * whose storage comes from the kernel heap.  CONFIG_RAM_SIZE is 344064
9:  * bytes and at the time the SRAM heap held roughly 300KB of that, while one
10:  * 640x480 YUYV frame is 614400 bytes -- so `output /tmp/frame.yuv 1` could
11:  * never succeed, the write() always failed with ENOMEM.  This board does,
12:  * however, have 16MB of PSRAM, so a RAM disk carved out of PSRAM gives the
13:  * filesystem enough room for several full frames without touching the SRAM
14:  * heap at all.
15:  *
16:  * Since "fix(psram): give the system heap the unused tail of PSRAM_SECTION"
17:  * the system heap itself reaches into PSRAM (6.4MB arena), so tmpfs is no
18:  * longer categorically too small.  This ramdisk is still the better place for
19:  * frame-sized files: it does not compete with task stacks and allocations for
20:  * the same free blocks, and its 2MB is bounded and predictable.
21:  *
22:  * Usage after boot (the ramdisk is registered but intentionally left
23:  * unformatted, since its contents are volatile anyway):
24:  *
25:  *   mkfatfs /dev/ram0
26:  *   mount -t vfat /dev/ram0 /mnt
27:  *   nxcamera
28:  *     input /dev/video0
29:  *     output /mnt/frame.yuv 1     <- exactly one frame, then stream stops
30:  *     stream 640 480 30 YUYV
31:  *     q
32:  *   ls -l /mnt
33:  *   hexdump /mnt/frame.yuv count=64
34:  *
35:  * The .yuv file is raw YUYV (YUV422), so on a host it converts with e.g.
36:  *   ffmpeg -f rawvideo -pix_fmt yuyv422 -s 640x480 -i frame.yuv frame.png
37:  *
38:  * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
39:  ****************************************************************************/
40: 
41: #include <nuttx/config.h>
42: 
43: #include <stdint.h>
44: #include <stdio.h>
45: #include <errno.h>
46: 
47: #include <nuttx/drivers/ramdisk.h>
48: #include <nuttx/fs/fs.h>
49: 
50: #include "bk7258_psram.h"
51: #include "bk7258_ramdisk.h"
52: 
53: /****************************************************************************
54:  * Pre-processor Definitions
55:  ****************************************************************************/
56: 
57: #define BK7258_RAMDISK_MINOR      0
58: #define BK7258_RAMDISK_SECTOR     512u
59: 
60: /* Where it gets mounted.  Keep this in step with
61:  * CONFIG_EXAMPLES_AI_AGENT_VELA_DATA_DIR in configs/ai_agent/defconfig, whose
62:  * value is "/mnt/ai_agent": the agent creates the ai_agent/ subtree itself,
63:  * but only if the mount point below is a real filesystem.
64:  */
65: 
66: #define BK7258_RAMDISK_MOUNTPT    "/mnt"
67: 
68: /* 2MB: enough for three 640x480 YUYV frames plus FAT overhead, out of the
69:  * 2.9MB AP PSRAM heap (BK7258_AP_PSRAM_HEAP_*, bk7258_psram.c).  The V4L2
70:  * capture buffers do not come from this heap -- they are allocated from the
71:  * separate PSRAM DISPLAY pool by bk7258_camera_imgdata.c -- so the two do
72:  * not compete.
73:  */
74: 
75: #define BK7258_RAMDISK_BYTES      (2u * 1024u * 1024u)
76: #define BK7258_RAMDISK_SECTORS    (BK7258_RAMDISK_BYTES / BK7258_RAMDISK_SECTOR)
77: 
78: /****************************************************************************
79:  * Public Functions
80:  ****************************************************************************/
81: 
82: int bk7258_ramdisk_initialize(void)
83: {
84: #ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_PSRAM
85:   FAR uint8_t *buffer;
86:   int ret;
87: 
88:   if (!bk7258_psram_is_online())
89:     {
90:       printf("ramdisk: PSRAM offline, /dev/ram0 not registered\n");
91:       return -ENODEV;
92:     }
93: 
94:   buffer = bk7258_psram_memalign(BK7258_RAMDISK_SECTOR,
95:                                  BK7258_RAMDISK_BYTES);
96:   if (buffer == NULL)
97:     {
98:       printf("ramdisk: PSRAM allocation of %u bytes failed\n",
99:              (unsigned int)BK7258_RAMDISK_BYTES);
100:       return -ENOMEM;
101:     }
102: 
103:   ret = ramdisk_register(BK7258_RAMDISK_MINOR, buffer,
104:                          BK7258_RAMDISK_SECTORS, BK7258_RAMDISK_SECTOR,
105:                          RDFLAG_WRENABLED);
106:   if (ret < 0)
107:     {
108:       printf("ramdisk: ramdisk_register failed, error=%d\n", ret);
109:       bk7258_psram_free(buffer);
110:       return ret;
111:     }
112: 
113:   printf("ramdisk: /dev/ram0 registered, %u KB at %p (PSRAM)\n",
114:          (unsigned int)(BK7258_RAMDISK_BYTES / 1024u), buffer);
115: 
116:   /* Mount it, rather than leaving the mount to whoever remembers to type it.
117:    *
118:    * Applications that keep state ask for a path, not for a block device:
119:    * ai_agent's config store, memory store and skill loader all write under
120:    * CONFIG_EXAMPLES_AI_AGENT_VELA_DATA_DIR ("/mnt/ai_agent").  They do build
121:    * their directory tree themselves -- config_store.c's mkdirs() and
122:    * memory_store.c's ensure_dir() both walk the path -- but no amount of
123:    * mkdir() helps while /mnt is still pseudo-filesystem, so without this the
124:    * agent starts and then loses every skill and its whole config:
125:    *
126:    *   [skills] Cannot write skill: /mnt/ai_agent/skills/weather.md
127:    *
128:    * littlefs with -o autoformat is what makes this a one-liner: it formats
129:    * the device when the mount finds no valid superblock, which is exactly
130:    * right for a RAM disk whose contents are gone after every reset anyway.
131:    * FAT would need mkfatfs(), which lives in apps/fsutils and is not
132:    * reachable from board bring-up.
133:    *
134:    * This is not persistence.  The backing store is PSRAM, so the tree is
135:    * rebuilt from scratch on each boot; what it buys is that the agent's
136:    * paths are writable at all.  Real persistence needs a flash partition,
137:    * and when it arrives only the device name below has to change.
138:    */
139: 
140: #ifdef CONFIG_FS_LITTLEFS
141:   ret = nx_mount("/dev/ram0", BK7258_RAMDISK_MOUNTPT, "littlefs", 0,
142:                  "autoformat");
143:   if (ret < 0)
144:     {
145:       printf("ramdisk: mount %s failed, error=%d; format with "
146:              "\"mkfatfs /dev/ram0\" then \"mount -t vfat /dev/ram0 %s\"\n",
147:              BK7258_RAMDISK_MOUNTPT, ret, BK7258_RAMDISK_MOUNTPT);
148:       return OK;
149:     }
150: 
151:   printf("ramdisk: %s mounted (littlefs on /dev/ram0)\n",
152:          BK7258_RAMDISK_MOUNTPT);
153: #else
154:   printf("ramdisk: CONFIG_FS_LITTLEFS not set; format with "
155:          "\"mkfatfs /dev/ram0\" then \"mount -t vfat /dev/ram0 %s\"\n",
156:          BK7258_RAMDISK_MOUNTPT);
157: #endif
158: 
159:   return OK;
160: #else
161:   return -ENOTSUP;
162: #endif
163: }

229: static int sdio_wait_command(struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv, uint32_t cmd)
230: {
231:   clock_t deadline = clock_systime_ticks() + MSEC2TICK(1000);
232:   uint32_t status;
233: 
234:   for (;;)
235:     {
236:       status = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS);
237:       if ((status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
238:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
239:                      BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT)) != 0)
240:         {
241:           break;
242:         }
243: 
244:       if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - deadline) >= 0)
245:         {
246:           printf("SDIO CMD%u timeout status=0x%08lx\n",
247:                  (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
248:                  (unsigned long)status);
249:           return -ETIMEDOUT;
250:         }
251: 
252:       /* At transfer speed the RX FIFO can fill before a 100 us sleep
253:        * expires.  Keep the PIO loop tight while data is active; otherwise a
254:        * 512-byte sector consistently overflows after the first 256 bytes. */
255:       if (!priv->data_active)
256:         {
257:           nxsig_usleep(100);
258:         }
259:     }
260: 
261:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS,
262:              status & (BK7258_SDIO_CMD_NO_RESPONSE |
263:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_RESPONSE_END |
264:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT |
265:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_OK |
266:                        BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL));
267: 
268:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_TIMEOUT) != 0)
269:     {

271:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
272:              (unsigned long)status);
273:       return -ETIMEDOUT;
274:     }
275: 
276:   /* The BK7258 host reports CRC failure for the open-drain/long-response
277:    * identification commands even when the vendor stack accepts the response.
278:    * Armino explicitly tolerates this for ACMD41, CMD2 and CMD9.  Keep the
279:    * same compatibility rule while preserving CRC errors for normal R1/R7.
280:    */
281:   if ((status & BK7258_SDIO_CMD_CRC_FAIL) != 0 &&
282:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != SD_ACMDIDX41 &&
283:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX2 &&
284:       (cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK) != MMCSD_CMDIDX9)
285:     {
286:       printf("SDIO CMD%u CRC error status=0x%08lx\n",
287:              (unsigned)(cmd & MMCSD_CMDIDX_MASK),
288:              (unsigned long)status);
289:       return -EIO;
290:     }
291: 
292:   return OK;

454: static void sdio_clock(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, enum sdio_clock_e rate)
455: {
456:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
457: 
458:   if (rate == CLOCK_SDIO_DISABLED)
459:     {
460:       sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, 0);
461:       modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_GATE, 0);
462:     }
463:   else if (rate == CLOCK_IDMODE)
464:     {
465:       sdio_set_clock(priv, BK7258_SDIO_ID_CLOCK);
466:       modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, 0, BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_GATE);
467:     }
468:   else if (rate == CLOCK_SD_TRANSFER_1BIT)
469:     {
470:       sdio_set_clock(priv, BK7258_SDIO_TRANSFER_CLOCK);
471:       modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_GATE, 0);
472:     }
473: }

475: static int sdio_attach(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
476: {
477:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
478:   int ret;
479: 
480:   if (priv->irq_attached)
481:     {
482:       return OK;
483:     }
484: 
485:   ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SDIO, sdio_interrupt, priv);
486:   if (ret < 0)
487:     {
488:       return ret;
489:     }
490: 
491:   up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_SDIO);
492:   priv->irq_attached = true;
493:   return OK;
494: }

496: static void sdio_blocksetup(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev,
497:                             unsigned int blocklen, unsigned int nblocks)
498: {
499:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
500: 
501:   priv->blocklen = blocklen;
502:   priv->nblocks = nblocks;
503: }

505: static int sdio_recvsetup(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, FAR uint8_t *buffer,
506:                           size_t nbytes)
507: {
508:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
509:   uint32_t value;
510: 
511:   if (buffer == NULL || nbytes == 0 || priv->blocklen == 0 ||
512:       priv->nblocks == 0 || nbytes != (priv->blocklen * priv->nblocks))
513:     {
514:       return -EINVAL;
515:     }
516: 
517:   /* Match the vendor read setup order: program timeout and clear stale W1C
518:    * status before asserting the RX FIFO and SD state resets. */
519:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMER, BK7258_SDIO_TIMEOUT);
520:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, 0xffffffffu);
521:   while (nxsem_trywait(&priv->data_sem) == OK)
522:     {
523:     }
524: 
525:   /* Complete the vendor V2 reset pulse before configuring the receive
526:    * transaction. */
527:   value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
528:   value &= ~(0xffffu | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
529:              BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_TX_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET);
530:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
531: 
532:   value |= 0x0101u | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
533:            BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_RECOVERY;
534:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
535: 
536:   value = ((priv->blocklen << BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_SHIFT) &
537:            BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK) | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BYTE_SELECT;
538:   /* BK7258 V2 uses its multi-block data engine for 512-byte reads even when
539:    * the card command is CMD17. Short register transfers such as SCR remain
540:    * in single-block mode. */
541: 
542:   if (priv->blocklen == 512)
543:     {
544:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_DATA_MULTIBLOCK;
545:     }
546:   /* Keep configuration and start as separate writes, matching the vendor
547:    * set_read_multi_block_data()/start_receive_data() sequence. */
548:   priv->buffer = buffer;
549:   priv->remaining = nbytes;
550:   priv->irq_status = 0;
551:   priv->data_result = -EINPROGRESS;
552:   priv->data_active = true;
553:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value);
554:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_INT_MASK, 0,
555:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
556:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT);
557:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_ENABLE);
558: 
559:   /* The vendor card driver requires this settling interval after starting
560:    * the receive engine; without it the receive-end event can be missed. */
561: 
562:   nxsig_usleep(2000);
563:   return OK;
564: }

582:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT, 0);
583:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, 0xffffffffu);
584:   priv->data_active = false;
585:   priv->buffer = NULL;

587:   priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
588:   priv->data_result = -ECANCELED;

595: {

598:   priv->wait_events = eventset;
599:   priv->wake_events = 0;

603: static int sdio_drain_fifo(FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv)
604: {
605:   while (priv->remaining != 0)
606:     {
607:       uint32_t word;
608:       unsigned int timeout = 400;
609:       size_t copy = priv->remaining < sizeof(word) ? priv->remaining :
610:                     sizeof(word);
611: 
612:       while ((sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO) & BK7258_SDIO_RX_READY) == 0 &&
613:              timeout-- != 0)
614:         {
615:           up_udelay(1);
616:         }
617: 
618:       if (timeout == 0)
619:         {
620:           return -EIO;
621:         }
622: 
623:       word = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_RX_FIFO);
624:       memcpy(priv->buffer, &word, copy);
625:       priv->buffer += copy;
626:       priv->remaining -= copy;
627:     }
628: 
629:   return OK;
630: }
631: 
632: static sdio_eventset_t sdio_eventwait(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev)
633: {
634:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
635:   uint32_t status;
636:   int ret;
637: 
638:   if ((priv->wait_events & SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT) != 0)
639:     {
640:       ret = nxsem_tickwait_uninterruptible(&priv->data_sem,
641:                                             MSEC2TICK(priv->wait_timeout));
642:     }
643:   else
644:     {
645:       ret = nxsem_wait_uninterruptible(&priv->data_sem);
646:     }
647: 
648:   status = priv->irq_status;
649:   if (ret < 0)
650:     {
651:       priv->data_active = false;
652:       priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT;
653:       printf("SDIO data wait timeout status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu\n",
654:              (unsigned long)sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS),
655:              (unsigned long)priv->remaining);
656:     }
657:   else if (priv->data_result < 0)
658:     {
659:       priv->wake_events = priv->data_result == -ETIMEDOUT ? SDIOWAIT_TIMEOUT :
660:                           SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
661:       printf("SDIO data error=%d status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu\n",
662:              priv->data_result, (unsigned long)status,
663:              (unsigned long)priv->remaining);
664:     }
665:   else if (sdio_drain_fifo(priv) == OK && priv->remaining == 0)
666:     {
667:       priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_TRANSFERDONE;
668:     }
669:   else
670:     {
671:       priv->wake_events = SDIOWAIT_ERROR;
672:       printf("SDIO FIFO drain failed status=0x%08lx remaining=%lu\n",
673:              (unsigned long)status, (unsigned long)priv->remaining);
674:     }
675: 
676:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_INT_MASK,
677:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
678:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT, 0);
679:   sdio_reset_data_state();
680: 
681:   priv->wait_events = 0;
682:   priv->buffer = NULL;
683:   priv->remaining = 0;
684:   return priv->wake_events;
685: }

1: # VelaSight 随行 AI 智能眼镜：BK7258 OpenVela 适配
2: 
3: ## 一、作品简介
4: 
5: 本项目将 OpenVela/NuttX 移植到 BK7258 三核平台，以物理 CPU1/CPU2 运行
6: OpenVela AP，保留物理 CPU0 上的 Armino CP、Bootloader、无线控制器和标准打包
7: 流程。在此基础上接入 Mailbox 控制台、Wi-Fi、相机、音频、显示、振动反馈和板载
8: SD-NAND，为随行 AI 智能眼镜提供可复现的系统底座。
9: 
10: 项目当前已完成 AP 双核启动、单 UART0 双向控制台、NuttX `wlan0` 网络链路、
11: Camera/Audio 基础门禁，以及板载 SD-NAND 的只读 MMCSD/VFAT 链路。SD-NAND
12: 保持 1-bit、PIO、只读模式，不启用 DMA、4-bit、格式化或写操作。
13: 
14: ## 二、选题方向
15: 
16: 本作品属于 **新硬件适配** 方向，同时承载 AI 硬件产品验证。主要工作不是将应用
17: 简单部署到现成开发板，而是完成 BK7258 Cortex-M33 AP 的启动、中断、内存、SMP、
18: 跨核 Mailbox、板级外设和 OpenVela 子系统接入，并保留可重复构建和烧录的 CP/AP
19: 组合固件流程。
20: 
21: 主要技术特点：
22: 
23: - 物理 CPU0 运行 Armino CP，物理 CPU1/CPU2 运行 OpenVela/NuttX SMP。
24: - AP 日志和 NSH 输入输出通过 Mailbox V2 转发到 CP UART0，无需额外 USB-TTL。
25: - Wi-Fi controller 保留在 CP，OpenVela AP 提供 NuttX `wlan0` 和网络协议栈。
26: - SD-NAND 通过 BK7258 SDIO Host 接入 NuttX MMCSD，提供只读 VFAT 访问。
27: - 最终固件通过 Beken 标准分区和 packager 生成 `all-app.bin`。
28: 
29: ## 三、目录结构
30: 
31: ```text
32: app/                         比赛应用与板级验证命令
33: board/beken/                 BK7258 OpenVela 芯片层和板级适配
34: external/bk_avdk_smp/        可复现的 Armino CP 覆盖文件
35: docs/                        构建说明、移植方案、验收记录和参考资料
36: docs/plans/                  7 份活跃实施方案
37: docs/archive/                未启动或已归档的历史方案与工具说明
38: docs/reference/              OpenVela 官方移植文档的本地参考副本
39: logs/                        按大赛格式导出的 AI Coding 日志
40: .claude/skills/autoflash/    自动烧录操作技能
41: autoflash.sh                 BK7258 固件自动烧录脚本
42: ```
43: 
44: 文档入口：
45: 
46: - [固件构建步骤](docs/固件构建步骤.md)
47: - [项目技能规范](docs/SKILLS.md)
48: - [GitHub 开发指南](docs/github开发指南.md)
49: - [基础适配门禁验收记录](docs/8.16基础适配门禁验收记录.md)
50: - [Wi-Fi 使用说明](docs/WiFi使用说明.md)
51: - [移植方案索引](docs/plans/README.md)
52: 
53: ## 四、构建、烧录与运行
54: 
55: ### 4.1 工作区布局
56: 
57: 本项目需要比赛仓、OpenVela 工作树和 Beken AVDK SMP 工程：
58: 
59: ```text
60: /home/mi/vela_competition/
61: ├── contest/
62: │   └── contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/
63: └── bk_avdk_smp/
64: ```
65: 
66: 先按 [external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md](external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md) 将比赛仓中的
67: CP 权威覆盖文件同步到 `bk_avdk_smp`，并执行逐字节校验。
68: 
69: ### 4.2 构建 OpenVela AP
70: 
71: ```bash
72: cd /home/mi/vela_competition/contest
73: 
74: ./build.sh \
75:   vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh \
76:   --cmake distclean
77: 
78: ./build.sh \
79:   vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh \
80:   -e -Werror \
81:   --cmake \
82:   -j8
83: ```
84: 
85: ### 4.3 打包最终固件
86: 
87: ```bash
88: cp /home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.bin \
89:   /home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/build/openvela-ap.bin
90: 
91: cd /home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp
92: podman run --rm \
93:   --userns=keep-id \
94:   -v "$PWD:/armino" \
95:   -w /armino \
96:   localhost/bekencorp/armino-idk:1.5 \
97:   make -C projects/app_ab bk7258 \
98:   SDK_DIR=/armino \
99:   EXTERNAL_AP_BIN=/armino/build/openvela-ap.bin
100: ```
101: 
102: 完整步骤、产物路径和哈希校验见 [docs/固件构建步骤.md](docs/固件构建步骤.md)。
103: 
104: ### 4.4 烧录和控制台
105: 
106: ```bash
107: cd /home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing
108: ./autoflash.sh -p /dev/ttyUSB1 -n 1
109: ```
110: 
111: 连接开发板 UART0 后，在 CP 命令行进入 AP NSH：
112: 
113: ```text
114: ap_console status
115: ap_console open

564: | sector 0 直接是 FAT boot sector | `/dev/mmcsd0` |
565: | MBR + FAT 分区 | 自定义注册 `/dev/mmcsd0p0` 等 |
566: | protective MBR + LBA1 `EFI PART` | 启用 GPT parser 后注册产品定义路径 |
567: | 无合法结构 | 停止，不写入，不格式化 |
568: 
569: P0 门禁：硬件 pin、VCC、容量、SD response、sector layout 和 owner 全部有证据。
570: 
571: ### 5.3 P1：PWC clock request 和 Host MMIO
572: 
573: 先不要写 lower-half。根据 CP handler 和 mailbox 抓包确认：
574: 
575: ```text
576: SDIO clock/power command ID
577: SDIO module ID
578: ON/OFF 参数编码
579: transport ACK
580: semantic ACK/result/version
581: timeout 和拒绝行为
582: ```
583: 
584: 当前 AP 只有 `bk7258_pwc_start()` 和 PSRAM 语义；不要假设可直接调用
585: `bk7258_pwc_clock_request()`。新增接口应满足：
586: 
587: ```text
588: bk7258_pwc_clock_request(CLK_PWR_ID_SDIO, ON, timeout)
589:     -> serialize PWC request
590:     -> wait transport ACK
591:     -> wait semantic ACK or validated gate readback
592:     -> success only then access 0x458d0000
593: ```
594: 
595: PWC 请求只能在 task context，不能从 SDIO ISR 发起。失败必须使初始化返回错误，
596: 不得用固定 delay 代替 ACK/readback。P1 门禁：100 次冷启动均能得到确定的成功
597: 或有限超时，且 clock request 失败时无 SDIO MMIO 访问。
598: 
599: ### 5.4 P2：IRQ、pinmux、reset 和 command-only
600: 
601: 新增 IRQ 定义：
602: 
603: ```c
604: #define BK7258_EXTIRQ_SDIO 10
605: #define BK7258_IRQ_SDIO    (BK7258_IRQ_FIRST + BK7258_EXTIRQ_SDIO)
606: ```
607: 
608: 同时实现并验证：
609: 
610: ```text
611: CPU1 route bit 10
612: NVIC IRQ 26
613: irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_SDIO, ...)
614: up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_SDIO)
615: ```
616: 
617: 先实现 `reset`、`clock`、`attach`、`sendcmd`、`waitresponse` 和 response readers，
618: 不注册 FAT、不启用 data path。按 CMD0、CMD8、ACMD41、CMD2、CMD3、CMD9、CMD7
619: 顺序验证。P2 门禁：CID/CSD/OCR 与 golden 一致；无卡或断电时有限 timeout，
620: 不得 hard fault 或无限等待。
621: 
622: ### 5.5 P3：PIO RX、MMCSD bind 和只读 block 验证
623: 
624: 实现 `blocksetup`、`recvsetup`、`waitenable`、`eventwait`、`cancel`，先支持：
625: 
626: ```text
627: 8-byte SCR
628: 512-byte CMD17
629: 任意 alignment 的 destination
630: ```
631: 
632: 然后 board 层执行：
633: 
634: ```c
635: dev = bk7258_sdio_initialize(0);
636: ret = mmcsd_slotinitialize(0, dev);
637: ```
638: 
639: 固定介质的 `status()` 返回 `SDIO_STATUS_PRESENT`。`registercallback()` 保存
640: NuttX `worker_t` 和 arg，`callbackenable()` 不伪造 card removal。成功探测后
641: 检查 `/dev/mmcsd0` 是否出现；不要把 `mmcsd_slotinitialize()` 返回成功等同于
642: block node 已注册。
643: 
644: P3 门禁：能够读 geometry、sector 0 和测试 LBA；sector hash 与原厂一致；连续
645: 和随机只读无 CRC、timeout、overflow；错误 cancel 后可以继续发 command。
646: 
647: ### 5.6 P4：PIO TX 和受控写验证
648: 
649: 只有完成备份并确认专用测试 LBA 后才实现 write。首版只做 CMD24 单块写：
650: 
651: ```text
652: 清 stale status
653: 配置 block size/data timer
654: TX ready prime FIFO
655: sendsetup
656: enable TX watermark/write-end/error IRQ
657: 等待 DATA_WR_END 和 accepted write response
658: ```
659: 
660: 使用 zero、ones、walking bit、PRNG 和 unaligned source 做写回读验证。生产
661: FAT 卷不能执行 `cmocka_driver_block` 或破坏性 block test。P4 门禁：至少 10,000
662: 次随机单块读写无 silent corruption，错误后 reset/cancel 可恢复。
663: 
664: ### 5.7 P5：FAT/VFAT 只读挂载
665: 
666: 先根据 P0 布局选择 whole-disk 或自定义 partition device。superfloppy 可直接
667: 挂载 `/dev/mmcsd0`；MBR/GPT 必须先启用对应 parser 并通过 `parse_block_partition()`
668: 调用 `register_blockpartition()` 注册路径。NuttX 不会自动产生 `/dev/mmcsd0p0`。
669: 
670: NuttX 配置：
671: 
672: ```text
673: CONFIG_MMCSD=y
674: CONFIG_MMCSD_SDIO=y
675: CONFIG_MMCSD_NSLOTS=1
676: CONFIG_MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1
677: # CONFIG_MMCSD_SPI is not set
678: # CONFIG_MMCSD_MMCSUPPORT is not set
679: # CONFIG_MMCSD_HAVE_CARDDETECT is not set
680: # CONFIG_MMCSD_HAVE_WRITEPROTECT is not set
681: CONFIG_SDIO_BLOCKSETUP=y
682: # CONFIG_SDIO_DMA is not set
683: CONFIG_FS_FAT=y
684: # CONFIG_FSUTILS_MKFATFS is not set
685: CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK=y
686: ```
687: 
688: 按实际布局追加且只追加需要的配置：
689: 
690: ```text
691: CONFIG_MBR_PARTITION=y
692: ```
693: 
694: 或：
695: 
696: ```text
697: CONFIG_GPT_PARTITION=y
698: ```
699: 
700: 挂载命令：
701: 
702: ```text
703: mount -t vfat /dev/mmcsd0 /mnt/sdnand
704: ```
705: 
706: 有分区时将 source 替换为实际注册的 `/dev/mmcsd0p0`。首次只执行 `mount`、
707: `ls`、文件长度和 hash 对比，不执行 `mkfatfs`、`fsck` 自动修复或写操作。
708: 
709: P5 门禁：原厂目录和文件 hash 一致，挂载/卸载 100 次稳定，原有 FAT 数据无损。
710: 
711: ### 5.8 P6：受控文件写和掉电
712: 
713: 按以下顺序测试：
714: 
715: ```text
716: create -> write -> fsync -> read -> rename -> unlink
717: ```
718: 
719: 覆盖 0-byte、小文件、大文件、空间耗尽、重复 mount/unmount 和并发日志/Wi-Fi/
720: BT 负载。正常掉电前执行：
721: 
722: ```text
723: 阻止新 writer
724: fsync 所有文件
725: sync filesystem
726: unmount
727: 等待 active transfer 完成
728: CMD13 确认 card 不 busy
729: 遵守器件 datasheet 的 power-off delay
730: ```
731: 
732: 没有器件型号和 datasheet 前，不声明 write cache 的掉电安全性。至少执行 idle、
733: write 中、fsync 后、unmount 后四类受控断电测试。
734: 
735: ### 5.9 P7：multiblock 和 4-bit PIO（可选）
736: 
737: multiblock 先单独解除 `CONFIG_MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1`，验证 CMD18/CMD25/
738: CMD12、2/4/8/32/128 sectors 和错误恢复。通过后再评估 4-bit：
739: 
740: 1. 1-bit 6.5/13 MHz 长稳。
741: 2. 1-bit 20 MHz 长稳。
742: 3. watermark IRQ 压力测试。
743: 4. `capabilities()` 从 `SDIO_CAPS_1BIT_ONLY` 改为 `SDIO_CAPS_4BIT`。
744: 5. 由 MMCSD 上层读取 SCR、发送 ACMD6，lower-half 的 `widebus()` 只改 Host width。
745: 6. 4-bit 先低速，最后评估 20 MHz。
746: 
747: 若 4-bit PIO 在高负载下失败，交付可靠的 1-bit，不引入未适配 SDIO DMA。

753: 当前 `defconfig` 顶部注明由 menuconfig 生成。修改配置时以该文件所属配置为
754: 输入，通过 menuconfig 或 `savedefconfig` 更新，不手工维护生成的 `.config`。
755: 首版必须移除 `CONFIG_FSUTILS_MKFATFS=y`。保留已有的 `CONFIG_FS_FAT=y`，并
756: 加入 MMCSD/SDIO 配置；`CONFIG_DMA` 是否因其他外设需要保持开启，不影响本计划，
757: 但 `CONFIG_SDIO_DMA` 必须关闭。

A delayed in-place swap of `/mnt` is unsafe: by five seconds applications can already hold files or directories on LittleFS, and NuttX unmount may correctly return `-EBUSY`. The minimal stable namespace is therefore volatile `/mnt` plus persistent `/mnt/sdnand`, with persistent consumers explicitly configured for `/mnt/sdnand/...`; I’m validating exact mount/unmount errno behavior and whether any app code hardcodes the old tree.

431:    * system returns a reference to some opaque, fs-dependent structure
432:    * that encapsulates this binding.
433:    */
434: 
435:   if (mops->bind == NULL)
436:     {
437:       /* The filesystem does not support the bind operation ??? */
438: 
439:       ferr("ERROR: Filesystem does not support bind\n");
440:       ret = -EINVAL;
441:       goto errout_with_lock;
442:     }
443: 
444:   /* Increment reference count for the reference we pass to the file system */
445: 
446: #if defined(BDFS_SUPPORT) || defined(MDFS_SUPPORT)
447: #ifdef NODFS_SUPPORT
448:   if (drvr_inode != NULL)
449: #endif
450:     {
451:       atomic_add(&drvr_inode->i_crefs, 1);
452:     }
453: #endif
454: 
455:   inode_unlock();
456: 
457:   /* On failure, the bind method returns -errorcode */
458: 
459: #if defined(BDFS_SUPPORT) || defined(MDFS_SUPPORT)
460:   ret = mops->bind(drvr_inode, data, &fshandle);
461: #else
462:   ret = mops->bind(NULL, data, &fshandle);
463: #endif
464:   inode_lock();
465:   if (ret < 0)
466:     {
467:       /* The inode is unhappy with the driver for some reason.  Back out
468:        * the count for the reference we failed to pass and exit with an
469:        * error.
470:        */
471: 
472:       ferr("ERROR: Bind method failed: %d\n", ret);
473: 
474: #if defined(BDFS_SUPPORT) || defined(MDFS_SUPPORT)
475: #ifdef NODFS_SUPPORT
476:       if (drvr_inode != NULL)
477: #endif
478:         {
479:           atomic_sub(&drvr_inode->i_crefs, 1);
480:         }
481: #endif
482: 
483:       goto errout_with_lock;
484:     }
485: 
486:   /* Insert a dummy node -- we need to hold the inode semaphore
487:    * to do this because we will have a momentarily bad structure.
488:    * NOTE that the new inode will be created with an initial reference
489:    * count of zero.
490:    */
491: 
492:   if (mountpt_inode == NULL)
493:     {
494:       ret = inode_reserve_path(target, 0777, &mountpt_inode);
495:       if (ret < 0)
496:         {
497:           /* inode_reserve can fail for a couple of reasons, but the most
498:            * likely one is that the inode already exists. inode_reserve may
499:            * return:
500:            *
501:            *  -EINVAL - 'path' is invalid for this operation
502:            *  -EEXIST - An inode already exists at 'path'
503:            *  -ENOMEM - Failed to allocate in-memory resources for the
504:            *            operation
505:            */
506: 
507:           ferr("ERROR: Failed to reserve inode for target %s\n", target);
508:           goto errout_with_bind;
509:         }
510:     }
511: 
512:   /* We have it, now populate it with driver specific information. */
513: 
514:   INODE_SET_MOUNTPT(mountpt_inode);
515: #ifdef CONFIG_FS_PATHCACHE
516:   if (data != NULL && strstr(data, "pathcache") != NULL)
517:     {
518:       INODE_ENABLE_PATHCACHE(mountpt_inode);
519:     }
520: #endif
521: 
522:   mountpt_inode->u.i_mops  = mops;
523:   mountpt_inode->i_private = fshandle;
524:   inode_unlock();
525: 
526:   /* We can release our reference to the blkdrver_inode, if the filesystem
527:    * wants to retain the blockdriver inode (which it should), then it must
528:    * have called inode_addref().  There is one reference on mountpt_inode
529:    * that will persist until umount2() is called.
530:    */
531: 
532: #if defined(BDFS_SUPPORT) || defined(MDFS_SUPPORT)
533: #ifdef NODFS_SUPPORT
534:   if (drvr_inode != NULL)
535: #endif
536:     {
537:       inode_release(drvr_inode);
538:     }
539: #endif
540: 
541: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PSEUDOFS_OPERATIONS
542:   RELEASE_SEARCH(&desc);
543: #endif
544: #ifdef CONFIG_FS_NOTIFY
545:   notify_create(target);
546: #endif
547:   return OK;
548: 
549:   /* A lot of goto's!  But they make the error handling much simpler */
550: 
551: errout_with_bind:
552:   if (mops->unbind != NULL)
553:     {
554:       mops->unbind(fshandle, &drvr_inode, 0);
555:     }
556: 
557: errout_with_lock:
558:   inode_unlock();
559: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PSEUDOFS_OPERATIONS
560:   RELEASE_SEARCH(&desc);
561: #endif
562: 
563: errout_with_inode:
564: #if defined(BDFS_SUPPORT) || defined(MDFS_SUPPORT)
565:   if (drvr_inode != NULL)
566:     {
567:       inode_release(drvr_inode);
568:     }
569: #endif
570: 
571: errout:
572:   return ret;
573: 
574: #else
575:   ferr("ERROR: No filesystems enabled\n");
576:   return -ENOSYS;
577: #endif /* BDFS_SUPPORT || MDFS_SUPPORT || NODFS_SUPPORT */
578: }

45:  * Name: nx_umount2
46:  *
47:  * Description:
48:  *   nx_umount2() is similar to the standard 'umount2' interface except that
49:  *   is not a cancellation point and it does not modify the errno variable.
50:  *
51:  *   nx_umount2() is an internal NuttX interface and should not be called
52:  *   from applications.
53:  *
54:  * Returned Value:
55:  *   Zero is returned on success; a negated value is returned on any failure.
56:  *
57:  ****************************************************************************/
58: 
59: int nx_umount2(FAR const char *target, unsigned int flags)
60: {
61:   FAR struct inode *mountpt_inode;
62:   FAR struct inode *blkdrvr_inode = NULL;
63:   struct inode_search_s desc;
64:   int ret;
65: 
66:   /* Verify required pointer arguments */
67: 
68:   if (!target)
69:     {
70:       ret = -EFAULT;
71:       goto errout;
72:     }
73: 
74:   /* Find the mountpt */
75: 
76:   SETUP_SEARCH(&desc, target, false);
77: 
78:   ret = inode_find(&desc);
79:   if (ret < 0)
80:     {
81:       goto errout_with_search;
82:     }
83: 
84:   /* Get the search results */
85: 
86:   mountpt_inode = desc.node;
87:   DEBUGASSERT(mountpt_inode != NULL);
88: 
89:   /* Verify that the inode is a mountpoint */
90: 
91:   if (!INODE_IS_MOUNTPT(mountpt_inode))
92:     {
93:       ret = -EINVAL;
94:       goto errout_with_mountpt;
95:     }
96: 
97:   /* Unbind the block driver from the file system (destroying any fs
98:    * private data.
99:    */
100: 
101:   if (!mountpt_inode->u.i_mops->unbind)
102:     {
103:       /* The filesystem does not support the unbind operation ??? */
104: 
105:       ret = -EINVAL;
106:       goto errout_with_mountpt;
107:     }
108: 
109:   /* The unbind method returns the number of references to the
110:    * filesystem (i.e., open files), zero if the unbind was
111:    * performed, or a negated error code on a failure.
112:    */
113: 
114:   /* Hold the semaphore through the unbind logic */
115: 
116:   inode_lock();
117: #ifdef CONFIG_FS_PATHCACHE
118:   if (INODE_IS_PATHCACHE(mountpt_inode))
119:     {
120:       /* Invalidate all pathcache entries belonging to this mountpoint */
121: 
122:       pathcache_umount(mountpt_inode);
123:     }
124: #endif
125: 
126:   ret = mountpt_inode->u.i_mops->unbind(mountpt_inode->i_private,
127:                                        &blkdrvr_inode, flags);
128:   if (ret < 0)
129:     {
130:       /* The inode is unhappy with the blkdrvr for some reason */
131: 
132:       goto errout_with_lock;
133:     }
134:   else if (ret > 0)
135:     {
136:       ret = -EBUSY;
137:       goto errout_with_lock;
138:     }
139: 
140:   /* Successfully unbound.  Convert the mountpoint inode to regular
141:    * pseudo-file inode.
142:    */
143: 
144:   mountpt_inode->i_flags  &= ~FSNODEFLAG_TYPE_MASK;
145:   mountpt_inode->i_private = NULL;
146:   mountpt_inode->u.i_mops  = NULL;
147: 
148: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PSEUDOFS_OPERATIONS
149:   /* If the node has children, then do not delete it. */
150: 
151:   if (mountpt_inode->i_child != NULL)
152:     {
153:       /* Just decrement the reference count (without deleting it) */
154: 
155:       atomic_sub(&mountpt_inode->i_crefs, 1);
156:       inode_unlock();
157:     }
158:   else
159: #endif
160:     {
161:       /* Remove the mountpoint inode from the inode tree.  The inode will
162:        * not be deleted yet because there is still at least reference on
163:        * it (from the mount)
164:        */
165: 
166:       ret = inode_remove(target);
167:       inode_unlock();
168: 
169:       /* The return value of -EBUSY is normal (in fact, it should
170:        * not be OK)
171:        */
172: 
173:       if (ret != OK && ret != -EBUSY)
174:         {
175:           goto errout_with_mountpt;
176:         }
177: 
178:       /* Release the mountpoint inode and any block driver inode
179:        * returned by the file system unbind above.  This should cause
180:        * the inode to be deleted (unless there are other references)
181:        */
182: 
183:       inode_release(mountpt_inode);
184:     }
185: 
186:   /* Did the unbind method return a contained block driver */
187: 
188:   if (blkdrvr_inode)
189:     {
190:       inode_release(blkdrvr_inode);
191:     }
192: 
193:   RELEASE_SEARCH(&desc);
194: #ifdef CONFIG_FS_NOTIFY
195:   notify_unmount(target);
196: #endif
197:   return OK;
198: 
199:   /* A lot of goto's!  But they make the error handling much simpler */
200: 
201: errout_with_lock:
202:   inode_unlock();
203: 
204: errout_with_mountpt:
205:   inode_release(mountpt_inode);
206:   if (blkdrvr_inode)
207:     {
208:       inode_release(blkdrvr_inode);
209:     }
210: 
211: errout_with_search:
212:   RELEASE_SEARCH(&desc);
213: 
214: errout:
215:   return ret;
216: }
217: 
218: /****************************************************************************
219:  * Name: umount2
220:  *
221:  * Description:
222:  *   umount() detaches the filesystem mounted at the path specified by
223:  *  'target.'
224:  *
225:  * Returned Value:
226:  *   Zero is returned on success; -1 is returned on an error and errno is
227:  *   set appropriately:
228:  *
229:  *   EACCES A component of a path was not searchable or mounting a read-only
230:  *      filesystem was attempted without giving the MS_RDONLY flag.
231:  *   EBUSY The target could not be unmounted because it is busy.
232:  *   EFAULT The pointer argument points outside the user address space.
233:  *
234:  ****************************************************************************/
235: 
236: int umount2(FAR const char *target, unsigned int flags)
237: {
238:   int ret;
239: 
240:   ret = nx_umount2(target, flags);
241:   if (ret < 0)
242:     {
243:       set_errno(-ret);
244:       ret = ERROR;
245:     }
246: 
247:   return ret;
248: }

text:
**Findings**

The repository has two separate storage paths today:

- Volatile PSRAM RAM disk: `/dev/ram0` mounted as LittleFS at `/mnt`.
- SD-NAND: `/dev/mmcsd0`, with MBR partition registration intended to produce `/dev/mmcsd0p0`, currently read-only and not automatically mounted.

The current RAM-disk mount is explicit in [`bk7258_ramdisk.c:57-76`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_ramdisk.c:57) and [`bk7258_ramdisk.c:140-152`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_ramdisk.c:140):

```text
/dev/ram0 -> LittleFS -> /mnt
```

It is created from a 2 MiB PSRAM allocation and is intentionally volatile. Bring-up invokes it after PSRAM initialization at [`bk7258_bringup.c:187-201`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:187).

SD-NAND initialization is already scheduled asynchronously on LPWORK at [`bk7258_bringup.c:166-173`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:166). The default delay is 5 seconds at [`bk7258-ap/Kconfig:48-56`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/Kconfig:48).

That satisfies the non-blocking bring-up requirement, but the current worker still performs a potentially long bounded probe in the background:

- Initial host/card probe can wait up to 7 seconds at [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:22-24`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:22).
- The worker calls `bk7258_mmcsd_initialize()` after the delay at [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:149-164`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:149).
- `bk7258_bringup()` does not wait for that work item.

**Current SD-NAND limitations**

The checked-in SDIO implementation cannot currently provide a writable filesystem:

- The host advertises `SDIO_STATUS_WRPROTECTED` at [`bk7258_sdio.c:442-446`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:442).
- `sendcmd()` rejects write commands with `-EROFS` at [`bk7258_sdio.c:302-305`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:302).
- `sendsetup()` is unimplemented and returns `-EOPNOTSUPP` at [`bk7258_sdio.c:566-573`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:566).
- The `nsh` configuration forces `CONFIG_MMCSD_READONLY=y` at [`nsh/defconfig:81-96`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:81).
- The project README explicitly describes SD-NAND as read-only at [`README.md:10-12`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/README.md:10).

Therefore, writable mounting cannot be enabled safely by merely removing `MS_RDONLY` from a mount call. The SDIO TX path, MMCSD write configuration, and controlled write validation must be completed first.

**Partition handling**

The current board code does the following:

1. Initializes SDIO and binds MMCSD at [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:55-73`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:55).
2. Waits for `/dev/mmcsd0` to appear at [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:75-100`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:75).
3. Parses the MBR at [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:102-109`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:102).
4. Registers each parsed partition as `/dev/mmcsd0pN` at [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:37-52`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:37).

The project has validated `/dev/mmcsd0p0` on hardware:

- Geometry: 512-byte sectors, 247808 sectors.
- MBR signature: `55aa`.
- VFAT read-only mount: `/dev/mmcsd0p0`.
- Evidence: [`BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:1364-1395`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:1364).

The partition parser does not guarantee that `/dev/mmcsd0p0` exists merely because parsing succeeded. The project plan correctly documents that partition devices must be explicitly registered at [`BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:664-709`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:664).

The current handler also ignores `register_blockpartition()` errors at [`bk7258_mmcsd.c:49-51`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:49). A product mount worker should explicitly probe the expected partition node before mounting it.

**Recommended mountpoint**

Use:

```text
/mnt                 volatile PSRAM LittleFS
/mnt/sdnand          persistent SD-NAND VFAT
/mnt/sdnand/ai_agent persistent agent data
/mnt/sdnand/captures optional persistent image output
```

The project’s own SDIO plan already recommends `/mnt/sdnand` at [`BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:700-709`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:700).

Do not replace `/mnt` with SD-NAND after delayed initialization. The existing `/mnt` LittleFS mount is an active application filesystem and changing it would create all of these problems:

- Existing `/mnt` files would refer to the old LittleFS namespace.
- Open files would prevent a normal unmount.
- NuttX FAT unmount returns `-EBUSY` when files remain open at [`fs_fat32.c:2307-2345`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/fat/fs_fat32.c:2307).
- Force unmount is explicitly documented as potentially losing data.
- Applications that start before SD-NAND readiness would create state on the wrong filesystem.

NuttX allows a child mount under an existing mounted filesystem. The target `/mnt/sdnand` can be created or reserved under `/mnt`; there is no need to unmount the parent `/mnt`. Mount behavior and source-device lookup are implemented at [`fs_mount.c:314-428`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/mount/fs_mount.c:314).

**Applications relying on `/mnt`**

1. **AI agent**

The board-specific configuration sets:

```text
CONFIG_EXAMPLES_AI_AGENT_VELA_DATA_DIR="/mnt/ai_agent"
```

at [`ai_agent/defconfig:70-76`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/ai_agent/defconfig:70).

The upstream agent expands that setting into config, memory, sessions, skills, capture, and related files at [`agent_config.h:84-96`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/include/agent_config.h:84) and [`agent_config.h:182-184`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/include/agent_config.h:182).

The relevant writers are:

- Config store: [`config_store.c:101-108`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/infra/config_store.c:101).
- Memory store: [`memory_store.c:89-145`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/core/memory_store.c:89).
- Built-in skills: [`skill_loader.c:246-258`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/tools/skill_loader.c:246).

These should be redirected to `/mnt/sdnand/ai_agent` for persistence.

There is also a hardcoded simulation/bootstrap path in [`agent_main.c:490-504`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/agent_main.c:490). It mounts `/data` as tmpfs and creates `/data/agent` regardless of the configured agent data directory. This does not currently control the configured `/mnt/ai_agent` writes, but it should be changed or guarded in the eventual implementation so the startup path does not report a misleading storage state or create unnecessary volatile directories.

2. **`social_cue`**

This application hardcodes:

```text
/mnt/ai_agent/skills
```

at [`social_cue_main.c:68-74`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/social_cue/social_cue_main.c:68).

It creates and writes the skill file at [`social_cue_main.c:528-549`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/social_cue/social_cue_main.c:528). This path must be changed consistently with the agent data directory, or the installed skill will remain volatile while the rest of the agent data is persistent.

3. **`camera_preview`**

It accepts arbitrary expression-source and JPEG-output paths:

- `src=` and `jpegout=` parsing: [`camera_preview_main.c:1999-2025`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c:1999).
- JPEG writing: [`camera_preview_main.c:2348-2367`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c:2348).
- Expression file reads: [`camera_preview_main.c:2372-2397`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/camera_preview/camera_preview_main.c:2372).

These do not require a fixed path change. Keep `/mnt/...` for volatile capture artifacts, or direct persistent output explicitly to `/mnt/sdnand/...`.

4. **`agent_camera`**

Its `out=<path>` argument is arbitrary; the documented example is `/mnt/cap.jpg` at [`agent_camera_main.c:47-50`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/packages/ai_agent/src/agent_main.c:47) and parsing occurs in the contest app at [`agent_camera_main.c:1237`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/agent_camera/agent_camera_main.c:1237). 5. **`periph_selftest`**

The storage self-test explicitly mounts `/dev/mmcsd0p0` or `/dev/mmcsd0` at `/mnt/sd` and later unmounts it:

- Mount: [`periph_selftest_main.c:177-192`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/periph_selftest/periph_selftest_main.c:177).
- Unmount: [`periph_selftest_main.c:193-220`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/periph_selftest/periph_selftest_main.c:193).

This does not collide with `/mnt/sdnand`, but it can fail with `-EBUSY` if the same block device is already mounted persistently. The self-test should either reuse the product mount, skip its temporary mount when `/mnt/sdnand` is active, or run before the product mount.

**Minimal architecture**

1. Keep the existing `/mnt` PSRAM LittleFS mount unchanged.
2. Add SD-NAND storage ownership and mount state to the existing delayed worker.
3. Initialize SDIO/MMCSD once. Do not repeatedly call `mmcsd_slotinitialize()` for every retry; the NuttX implementation allocates an MMCSD state object on each call at [`mmcsd_sdio.c:4561-4648`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:4561).
4. Let the existing SDIO/MMCSD callback mechanism perform media reprobe. The SDIO lower-half already has a recovery worker at [`bk7258_sdio.c:142-166`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:142).
5. Have a serialized mount worker retry only the readiness stages:
   - Probe `/dev/mmcsd0`.
   - Parse/register the known partition.
   - Confirm `/dev/mmcsd0p0` exists.
   - Attempt `nx_mount("/dev/mmcsd0p0", "/mnt/sdnand", "vfat", 0, NULL)`.
6. Use `/dev/mmcsd0` only for a validated super-floppy layout. Do not silently fall back to the whole disk after an invalid MBR. The project plan gives the correct layout decision table at [`BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:560-567`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:560).
7. Publish a storage-ready state only after the mount succeeds. Applications that require persistence must wait for this state or be started after it; they must not infer readiness merely from `/mnt` existing.
8. Change the agent data directory to `/mnt/sdnand/ai_agent` and update `social_cue` to use the same base.
9. Initially retain `CONFIG_MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1` and 1-bit PIO. Complete single-block write support before considering multiblock or 4-bit operation. The project plan specifies this sequencing at [`BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:647-662`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:647).

**Failure and retry semantics**

Classify failures as follows:

| Failure | Semantics |
|---|---|
| Host/PWC not ready, `/dev/mmcsd0` absent, `-ENODEV`, probe timeout, transient `-EIO` | Keep bring-up successful; leave SD-NAND state unavailable; retry with bounded backoff |
| `mmcsd_slotinitialize()` succeeds but node appears later | Do not call slot initialization again; reprobe node/partition and mount |
| MBR parse fails | Terminal for the current media layout; do not format or write; allow explicit diagnostic retry after media reset |
| Partition node missing after parser success | Retry registration/probe; report the registration error rather than assuming `/dev/mmcsd0p0` exists |
| FAT mount returns `-ENODEV`, `-ENOENT`, or transient I/O error | Leave `/mnt/sdnand` unmounted and retry |
| FAT superblock invalid or unsupported | Terminal data/layout error; do not autoformat production SD-NAND |
| Geometry reports write-disabled or lower-half rejects TX | Do not attempt writable mount; remain unavailable/read-only until driver/configuration is corrected |
| Mount succeeds | Mark persistent storage ready and stop the mount retry worker |

A normal unmount should be:

```text
stop new persistent writers
fsync open files
sync filesystem
nx_umount2("/mnt/sdnand", 0)
```

NuttX returns `-EBUSY` when FAT has open files at [`fs_fat32.c:2315-2345`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/fs/fat/fs_fat32.c:2315). Treat that as “still mounted; retry after clients close,” not as permission to force-detach.

Do not use `MNT_FORCE` for normal shutdown. The same code documents that forced unmount can cause data loss. The project’s SDIO plan also requires stopping writers, syncing, unmounting, waiting for transfers, checking card-not-busy, and only then powering down at [`BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:711-733`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/docs/plans/BK7258_OPENVELA_SDIO_PORTING_PLAN.md:711).

The current fixed-media implementation does not provide a complete hot-removal path:

- It always reports media present and write-protected at [`bk7258_sdio.c:442-446`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:442).
- MMCSD removal unregisters block nodes while mounted filesystems may still exist at [`mmcsd_sdio.c:4389-4429`](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/drivers/mmcsd/mmcsd_sdio.c:4389).

For the soldered SD-NAND, treat media removal or power loss as a controlled shutdown/error event: stop new writes, unmount if possible, and do not unregister or power-cycle the device while `/mnt/sdnand` remains busy.

**Verification matrix**

| Area | Required verification |
|---|---|
| Configuration | Unified AI-agent image enables `BK7258_SDIO`, `MMCSD`, `MMCSD_SDIO`, `FS_FAT`, MBR parser, and writable MMCSD; `MMCSD_READONLY=n`; SDIO DMA remains disabled initially |
| Bring-up | Console, mailbox, Wi-Fi, camera, and display become available without waiting for SD-NAND; delayed worker logs independently |
| Cold boot | 100 cold boots: success or bounded failure; no deadlock, hard fault, or AP bring-up abort |
| No-media/PWC failure | SD-NAND unavailable; bring-up remains usable; retries are bounded and observable |
| Enumeration | `/dev/mmcsd0` appears; geometry is 512-byte sectors; sector 0 matches the golden dump |
| Partition | MBR parsing registers `/dev/mmcsd0p0`; registration errors are checked; super-floppy fallback is used only for a validated super-floppy |
| Driver write path | Dedicated test LBA: single-block zero/ones/walking-bit/PRNG write, read-back, unaligned buffers, timeout/cancel recovery |
| FAT mount | Writable mount at `/mnt/sdnand`; `df`, `mkdir`, create, write, `fsync`, read, rename, unlink |
| Persistence | Write agent config, memory, and skill; reboot; verify `/mnt/sdnand/ai_agent/...` survives |
| `/mnt` collision | `/mnt` remains LittleFS; `/mnt/sdnand` is independently mounted; camera artifacts under `/mnt` still work |
| Self-test interaction | `periph_selftest` reuses or skips its `/mnt/sd` temporary mount when `/mnt/sdnand` is active |
| Unmount | Normal unmount succeeds after writers close; open-file unmount returns `-EBUSY`; no forced unmount in normal operation |
| Power loss | Controlled power interruption during idle, write, post-`fsync`, and post-unmount; verify FAT consistency and retained agent state |
| Long run | 24-hour read/write/hash loop, repeated mount/unmount, Wi-Fi/logging concurrency, and at least 100 reboot cycles |

The minimum viable persistent design is therefore: **writable SDIO TX support plus one-time MMCSD initialization, a retryable background mount worker, `/dev/mmcsd0p0` mounted at `/mnt/sdnand`, and explicit redirection of agent/social-cue data to `/mnt/sdnand/ai_agent` while retaining `/mnt` as the volatile PSRAM LittleFS filesystem.**
